reasoning:
**What is asked.** Nvidia's percent price return minus Microsoft's, from the close on Friday 20 November to the close on Friday 4 December 2026 (Yahoo Finance adjusted close), in percentage points.

**Starting point.** Both returns start from a close that has not happened yet, so today's prices tell me about volatility, not direction. Nobody reliably knows which of two liquid mega-caps will do better over nine trading days, so I centre on zero.

**Why the range is wide.** Nvidia is in an unusually turbulent stretch. It closed at $156.14 on 16 November 2026 (stockanalysis.com), down about 35% from $239.24 on 6 October, with daily moves of -9.3%, -4.3%, -5.5% and -4.1% inside two weeks. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on 12 November; CFO Colette Kress is interim chief and the board is searching for a successor (Kiplinger, 17 November). Results on 17 November beat expectations (revenue $115.8bn against about $108.8bn expected, next-quarter guide $130bn) and the shares rose about 4% after hours. Microsoft has been jumpy too: +6.7% on 4 November, -3.6% the next day, $523.88 on 13 November.

In calmer times I estimate this two-week gap has a standard deviation of about 6 points. With Nvidia's daily swings roughly double their usual size and leadership headlines still coming, I use about 8.5. The window has nine sessions (Thanksgiving closed, a half day on 27 November) and includes the November jobs report, due on 4 December. The Fed meets after it.

**What would move it.** A named successor, a return of Huang or findings from the board's investigation could move Nvidia 10% in a day either way. A broad relief rally would favour Nvidia, the higher-beta share. A further unwinding of AI positions would favour Microsoft.

**Forecast.** Median 0.0 points; middle half -5.3 to +5.3; 5th to 95th percentile -14 to +14, with about 8% beyond the ends of the -15 to +15 range.
question_title: How much will Nvidia's stock price returns exceed Microsoft's in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 23 - Dec 4)
